changes: ce_approx corrected 1762 → 1763: māgha of VS 1819 falls in Jan/Feb 1763 whether the year starts in Caitra or Kārttika
Premaśaṃkara's role changed from 'other' to 'scribe' (low confidence): 'lī' is read as the usual abbreviation for likhitam, as in western Indian colophons
Dīkpāla's confidence lowered to low: it may be a second person, part of Premaśaṃkara's name, or a corrupted family or caste name

notes: The era is not named; VS is assumed from the catalogue and from the Devanagari, western-Indian style of the colophon ('sudī'; Premaśaṅkara is a Gujarati-type name). 'līdā-' is read as 'li(khitaṃ) dā(sa?)', an abbreviation for likhitam, which would make Premaśaṃkara the scribe. This reading is uncertain. 'dīkpāla' may be a second person, part of the same name, or a corrupted surname; 'sajñāti' (= 'with kinsmen' or 'of the X jñāti/caste') is unclear. '(nāvarṣe)' perhaps stands for 'nāma varṣe', and '(ścamahīna)' is unclear. The verse 'śabdaśāstram anadhītya…' is a stock verse, not prosopographical.
